chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: Playing at Minton's and Monroe's Uptown House before and after Christian
summary: Collins sat in at Minton's with Joe Guy, Monk, Nick Fenton and Scotty, amid pimps following musicians, and his first recording was with Mildred Bailey.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: Did you play at Minton's before Charlie Christian arrived in New York?
Yeah, I used to go down there and play.
I heard Dizzy say you did. (Inaudible)
He said who was (Inaudible) playing at Minton's.

Sure, I used to go down there and play with them, you know. They had a nice little band there. It was Joe Guy, Monk, bass player Nick Fenton, who I got to work with us with Prez, also. And saxophone player by the name of Scotty. And it was like a hang out too, you know. We would go there, if you could get through the pimps. You know, they would always follow the musicians because of the chicks, you know.
The musicians drew the chicks and the chicks drew the pimps.
Then the chicks drew the pimps, you know, and they would try to take the chicks or whatever, you know. And we were primarily interested in playing any way.
Loved them, but I mean they had their place, you know.
Second. Second to the guitar. Second to Dizzy and Monk and Joe Guy, you know.
What about Scotty. Do you know his whole name?

You know, I can't think of Scotty's whole name, and Scotty was a tremendous saxophone player. He worked with Earl Hines after that for quite a while, and that's all we ever called him was Scotty. You know. But he just can't -- he's in San Francisco now, last time I saw him he was in San Francisco. But yes, I played at Minton's, yeah. Before and after.
Minton's-- Before you only Willie mentioned (inaudible) listening at
But Dizzy said you were part of the (inaudible) scene.
Well, I did but as I say, I would go down to listen because Charlie wouldn't be in there all the

time, you know, and whenever Charlie was going to be there I wouldn't listen any way because I loved to hear him play. You know, but I played at Minton's, the uptown House, at Monroe's uptown house, and -- because everybody went there. And I found -- I was listening to a record yesterday of Dinah, and it was -- the name of the tune was 'Where Are You.' That was the first recording I ever made and I made it with Mildred Bailey, in Chicago. That was one of the tunes I was trying to think of where you -- and she was quite -- that's another story. Mildred, she was quite a gal.
